test_title: SSC CPO 2023 Official Paper-II (Held On: 08 Jan, 2024)
subject: general
question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

Pay that bill today.

options.text: That bill will be paid today.
That bill is going to be paid today.
That bill should be paid today.
Let that bill to be paid today.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an imperative sentence which is used to give orders, commands, or instructions.
 
• In passive voice, we often use the structure "**let + object + be + past participle" **for imperative sentences.
 
• However, in this case, the correct form is to use "**should be"** **to convey the necessity of the action being completed.**
 
• Therefore, the correct passive form of "Pay that bill today." is "That bill should be paid today."

Hence, the correct passive voice is '***That bill should be paid today.'***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When converting imperative sentences into passive voice, the subject of the imperative verb becomes the object of the passive verb.
 
• For example,
 
 
• **Close the door = Let the door be closed.**
 
 
 
• However, not all imperative sentences follow this format, especially when conveying necessity or obligation.
 
• **In such cases, using "should be" or "must be" is appropriate for passive constructions.**
